precedence: Extends, does not replace, the 29-Nov-1943 through 15-Jan-1944 closeout.
guards: Increasing US Gilbert air/submarine pressure reduces daylight inter-atoll movement and raises abort/loss friction.
Late cargo mostly completes existing defense/base projects; it does not create new deep tunnel fortresses on coral atolls.
Personnel additions are bounded and must not be added again to later dated garrison totals.
personnel_note: Mostly engineers, aviation-base, signal/AA specialists and historically plausible final reinforcement fragments; not a new field formation.
construction_effect_by_31Jan: Priority bases finish more of already-started revetments, distributed magazines, generator/pump protection and alternate telephone routes.
Kwajalein/Roi lagoon-side fire plans and alternate command positions improve materially after Tarawa lessons, but flat-island depth remains the decisive ceiling.
Taroa/Wotje receive substantial work even if later bypassed because Japan does not know the exact US target.
Eniwetok improves as western staging/recovery node but remains less complete than Taroa or Kwajalein/Roi.
